applicabilityBasis.summary: Quill USDQ is a dollar-soft-pegged borrowing token on Scroll minted against WETH, wstETH, weETH or SCR collateral. The complete official FAQ says borrowed USDQ can fund anything including everyday expenses, so it is not merely a niche internal leverage unit. Protocol redemption yields underlying crypto collateral at dollar-equivalent value with a fee, not a demonstrated issuer promise to pay fixed national currency or bank-deposit monetary value. Marketing supports payment use but the legally obligated issuer and cash/deposit redemption elements are not established, leaving applicability unclear.

genius.notes: The website describes non-custodial algorithmic collateral operation. The governance documentation describes planned governance powers over fees, collateral and operating parameters; its future-tense wording does not establish completed decentralization or present implementation of those powers. No exact legal entity accepting USDQ monetary redemption obligations was identified. issuerEntity and issuerDomicile are omitted; neither a DAO label nor an interface brand is substituted for an issuer. Public reserve disclosure means protocol collateral/vault transparency, not confirmation of GENIUS-eligible reserves or reserve sufficiency. No public issuer 1:1 cash/deposit redemption policy or monthly independent reserve attestation was located in the checked disclosures; documented collateral/token redemption mechanics still exist. The Act remains pre-effective under the October 7, 2026 regime review: the September 30 SCRC procedural interim rule is not the comprehensive final-regulation trigger. General DASP restrictions begin July 18, 2028; foreign-offer lawful-order requirements follow Act effectiveness. No approval, unlawful status, whole-protocol exemption or registered foreign exception is inferred.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official pending application, foreign registration/comparability decision, or issuer-announced GENIUS intent naming Quill USDQ and Quill Finance was found in the opened implementation materials, NYDFS directory, protocol/legal disclosures and exact-name regulator-domain searches.
